name: Sense Field
label: Revelation
lede: A Harbor City hardcore band became one of the first emo bands on Revelation, sat out five years at Warner Bros., and still ended up playing Save Yourself for Jay Leno.

eras.title: A band that couldn't hold a lineup
eras.text: Jon Bunch and Chris Evenson spent the late '80s in Reason to Believe, a melodic hardcore band whose members kept leaving. In 1990 they quit fighting it and started over as Sense Field.

years.h: Jon Bunch and Chris Evenson start Reason to Believe
years.p: The melodic hardcore band makes two albums for Nemesis Records, The Next Door and When Reason Sleeps Demons Dance.
years.xp:
Bunch told No Echo the band began in 1986 after Evenson made a demo tape for school. They were listening to the Adolescents' Rick Agnew, Battalion of Saints, Poison Idea, Scream and Bad Religion.

Nemesis owner Frank Harrison got them on bills they wanted. "Big Frank did so much for our band," Bunch said.

q: Reason to Believe was plagued with lineup changes.
years.src: No Echo · Wikipedia: Sense Field · Revelation Records
years.h: Reason to Believe can't keep a lineup, so Sense Field starts
years.p: In Harbor City, California, Jon Bunch and Chris Evenson regroup with guitarist [[Rodney Sellars|28e2e039-5b35-4aa4-ab62-4457cf077abd]], bassist John Stockberger and drummer [[Scott McPherson|c857aba4-942d-448c-b172-7807647c648d]]. The new name comes with a slower, more open sound.
years.xp:
Bunch told No Echo that by 1990 the Los Angeles punk scene "felt dormant" to him. Peers like Jawbreaker, Samiam and Sunny Day Real Estate were already trying other directions.

Revelation's own bio credits Sense Field with pioneering the way for the emotional hardcore bands that followed.

eras.title: Jordan Cooper goes to a show
eras.text: Revelation co-founder Jordan Cooper saw Sense Field early and signed a Southern California band to a label best known for New York straight edge. By Building in 1996 they were touring with Far, Texas Is the Reason and Jimmy Eat World, and Warner Bros. was paying attention.

years.h: Jordan Cooper sees an early show and signs Sense Field
years.p: Revelation's co-founder brings a Harbor City band to the label. Bunch told No Echo that Cooper understood what they were.

years.h: Sense Field comes out as REV 037, in the middle of grunge
years.p: Revelation catalog number 037 is the self-titled album, out the same year as Killed for Less.

years.src: Wikipedia: Sense Field · No Echo · Revelation Records
years.h: Killed for Less is the debut, depending who's counting
years.p: Wikipedia lists it on Revelation in 1994, and Jon Bunch told No Echo it was the debut. Revelation's own catalog page doesn't list it.

eras.title: Signed to Warner, then forgotten
eras.text: Warner Bros. was supposed to be the step up. The label kept firing the people who had signed the band, Under the Radar sat on a shelf, and Sense Field waited out the rest of the '90s.

years.cap: Sense Field at the Euclid Tavern, Cleveland Heights, mid-1990s
years.src: Wikipedia: Sense Field · No Echo · Revelation Records
yt: Live at Coney Island High, New York, March 1996
years.p: It's Sense Field's last album on Revelation, and Warner signs the band the same year.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the Warner signing to 1996. Bunch said most of the people who brought the band to Warner were later fired, and Under the Radar never came out.

Revelation's bio puts the band on tour in these years with Far, Texas Is the Reason and Jimmy Eat World.

eras.title: The hit arrives late
eras.text: Nettwerk, a Canadian independent, picked the band up and the shelved Under the Radar songs came back re-recorded. Save Yourself got Sense Field on late-night TV more than a decade in. In 2004 they stopped.

years.h: Under the Radar never left Warner, so Tonight and Forever exists
years.p: Warner Bros. never released Under the Radar. Re-recorded, the songs became part of this Nettwerk album.
years.xp:
Bunch's account: "Most everyone at Warner that brought us to the label had been fired." Wikipedia puts the wait at five years. Warner eventually let the band out of the contract and let them re-record the songs elsewhere.

While he waited, Bunch told No Echo, he was working at a flower shop, delivering flowers.

yt: The Tonight Show with Jay Leno, April 15, 2002
years.h: Sense Field play Save Yourself for Jay Leno
years.p: The song lands on the Roswell soundtrack, then on The Late Late Show and The Tonight Show, and puts Jon Bunch and Chris Evenson in Rolling Stone.
years.xp:
The video uploads date the performances: The Late Late Show with Craig Kilborn on February 5, 2002, The Tonight Show with Jay Leno on April 15, 2002.

Bunch told No Echo the song is "about trying to be faithful when you're in a relationship."

years.h: Living Outside is the last album and the only one to chart
years.p: It reaches No. 37 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart.

years.cap: Sense Field at LOFT, Shinjuku, Tokyo, May 31, 2004
q: We stayed around too long. 13 years is a long time.
years.h: Sense Field call it after 13 years
years.p: Sense Field disband after Living Outside, 13 years after Reason to Believe became Sense Field.
years.xp: Bunch looked back for No Echo: "We stayed around too long. 13 years is a long time."

years.h: A week outside Orlando, and Jon Bunch has Hide Nothing
years.p: He joins [[Further Seems Forever|2bc3d11f-58fe-4adb-bfd9-6d316973005a]] as its third vocalist, sings on Hide Nothing and stays until 2006.
years.xp: Bunch told No Echo he wrote and recorded his vocals in one week outside Orlando: "I recorded the two I had written and then wrote a song a day."

eras.title: Reunions, then a benefit
eras.text: Revelation's 25th anniversary pulled bands back from across its catalog, Sense Field included. Four years later they played again without Jon Bunch, who had died, to raise money for his son.

years.cap: Sense Field at Revelation 25, Pomona, June 7, 2012
years.h: Sense Field come back for Revelation's 25th, in Pomona
years.p: Revelation pulls bands from across its catalog for anniversary shows, and Sense Field play the California one first.

years.h: Revelation 25 moves to Chicago, and Sense Field goes along
years.p: It's the second and last of the anniversary shows the band plays, seven months after Pomona.

years.cap: Sense Field at the Jon Bunch memorial benefit, Yost Theater, Santa Ana, March 20, 2016, with a guest singer up front
years.src: Broward Palm Beach New Times · Wikipedia: Jon Bunch
years.h: Jon Bunch, Sense Field's singer, dies at 45
years.p: He dies in Irvine, California, and the Orange County coroner rules it a suicide by overdose. He had been singing in Lucky Scars, after stints in War Generation and Further Seems Forever.
years.xp: The Broward Palm Beach New Times, reporting the coroner's findings, said the autopsy showed high levels of diphenhydramine, the antihistamine in over-the-counter sleeping pills, along with small amounts of alcohol and methamphetamine, and heart disease from high blood pressure. Investigators found empty sleeping-pill packs in his car.

years.src: Billy Penn · Broward Palm Beach New Times
years.h: Philadelphia fills the TLA for Jon Bunch's son
years.p: Sense Field reunite with guest singers at the TLA, on a bill with [[Texas Is the Reason|b93c736f-a82f-4cae-9e57-a60b12d7055f]] and [[Dag Nasty|4709dd69-1034-4634-9e88-d1099453b192]], to raise a college fund for Bunch's son. A first benefit had been held in Southern California.
years.xp:
Billy Penn reported fans and friends had already raised more than $65,000 for the college fund. Organizer Jeremy Weiss said "This is by no means a funeral...This is very much a rock concert."

Guest singers included Garrett Klahn, Dave Smalley, Ari Katz and Into Another's [[Richie Birkenhead|7a1a6273-c31b-4828-8e20-0d6ea66943aa]]. Rodney Sellars told Billy Penn: "the show is all about getting together to celebrate him."
